irregularities.text: The upload that created this repository contained only index.html, README.md, requirements.txt, conftest.py, .gitignore and .nojekyll. The assets/, data/, src/, scripts/ and docs/ trees of the original project were missing, so every script and the stylesheet returned 404 on GitHub Pages. The browser client, the harvest scripts, the data pipeline and this documentation were rebuilt in this repository.

The upstream repositories buffedlizard55-lab/LiveScoringErrors-Pending and buffedlizard55-lab/MLB-overturned-calls return HTTP 404. Nothing from them is copied into this site, and no claim made in the uploaded README is treated as evidence for a published value.

The uploaded README claims 22 run-removing plays and 28 runs removed across three seasons, plus 484 candidates. The harvest here derives 23 plays, 26 runs removed and 129 candidates from the official play-by-play of the same three seasons, and the three games the README names as examples reproduce exactly (745857 = 2 runs, 778307 = 2 runs, 823616 = 1 run). The README's season totals are not published because the README is not an official source and its candidate count cannot be reproduced; the per-play arithmetic on the official record is what the site publishes. The 2026 season also carries 5,954 automated pitch-challenge records, counted separately from reviews and never mixed into the run-removal list.

The game feed prints composite review codes such as NH and MJ, while MLB's review-reason registry publishes one- and two-letter reason codes (H = Home run, N = Fan interference, J = Pitch result). The site prints the raw feed code and names the reason only when the code's suffix exists in that registry; the leading letter, which is the review initiator, is not described because MLB does not publish it in that endpoint.

No pending ruling survives in the archived play-by-play for 2024-2026: MLB replaces the marker with the corrected call once the scorer rules, so the harvest returns zero cases and the field is reported as zero, not estimated. Detection uses only the two registered codes (os_ruling_pending_primary, os_ruling_pending_prior). The live view in the browser and the live-capture workflow are the only ways a case can be recorded; the archive starts empty by construction.

The 0-100 scoring model, its training corpus, model card, holdout metrics and correlation study were not part of the upload and are not reconstructed. No probability, Scoring Confidence Index or hypothetical RBI is published, because there is no model here that produced one. The rule the model would have had to satisfy is quoted from the Official Baseball Rules.

MLB's scoring-change page publishes the season it is currently listing, so the harvest covers 2026 only (255 entries, 63 with a stated before/after call). A before/after pair is published only when one official sentence names both sides of the change; 192 entries stay unclassified and are counted, never guessed. Entries may be revised or renumbered by MLB after publication; the official sentence is quoted on every row so a revision can be checked.

Each row links to the official play-by-play and to Baseball Savant's clip page for the play id read from the feed. The site does not re-host video and does not claim a clip was watched; the link is the official page for that play id, and MLB can retire a video.

The harvest covers completed regular-season, Wild Card, Division, LCS and World Series games for the seasons on file (2024-2026): 7,420 games, all of them scanned, none missing from the totals. Spring-training, exhibition and All-Star games are excluded, so a review in one of those games is not in the archive. Base occupancy is tracked from the official runner movements and required to agree with the score printed on every play and with the official final score in all 7,420 games; a game that fails either check publishes no count.
